# Joey in Sync

> Joey (Nikolaj Krištof Jochym) is a Discord community architect and author. He launches, repairs and staffs online communities, mostly on Discord: onboarding, governance, staff teams, events, growth and outreach, and the writing that holds it together. He works with game studios, Kickstarter creators and agencies. Seven years founding, running and directing communities. Open for work.

Every figure on this site comes from server message logs, member counts and dated announcement records. Case studies state what was measured and what was not.

## Who Joey works with

- [Game studios](https://joeyinsync.com/for/game-studios): a Discord built around the player journey — onboarding that sends players to the right channels, a feedback route from player report to a clear team decision and a visible status, and a staff team that runs it after handoff.
- [Kickstarter creators](https://joeyinsync.com/for/kickstarter): a home for backers — code-based backer access (the code from a backers-only update unlocks backer-only spaces; it does not check pledges), backer-only spaces, support tickets that keep purchase details out of public channels, feedback forums with status tags, and documentation for the team.
- [Agencies](https://joeyinsync.com/for/agencies): the Discord side of a client launch — a written scope the client approves, a server built to it, and a documented handoff (staff playbook and a 14-day engagement plan) the agency's or client's team can run.

## What clients hire Joey for

- Launch a community: server architecture and roles, launch plan and opening events, onboarding and first-contact flow, rules, moderation and security, initial staff structure.
- Fix a dying community: community audit and diagnosis, retention and channel restructure, feedback and reactivation loops, events and engagement systems, growth and partnership plan.
- Build a team that runs it: staff roles and departments, recruitment and application flows, training and operating standards, escalation and accountability, clean handoff and continuity.
- Growth and outreach: community research and lead sourcing, partnership development, Discord partnership outreach, creator and community collaborations, outreach tracking.

How a project runs: a review of the community or plan, an agreed written scope, then the build or the ongoing management.

## Case studies

- [Guildstew](https://joeyinsync.com/guildstew): paid client project. A Discord built for a Kickstarter community. Onboarding, backer access, support, feedback and staff operations in one server, handed over with practical documentation. Delivered October 2026.
- [Project Aurora](https://joeyinsync.com/aurora): a cold launch driven from 9 messages on day one to 2,508 on day fourteen, and the onboarding, governance, canon and security systems built to hold it. Joey started as Community Manager, Canon Director and consultant at once — he ran the community and the Discord's technical setup and wrote the entire lore — and was then promoted to Executive Director on the Aurora Board, leading the whole staff team. 2025–2026; the project is currently on hold.
- [Crimson Network](https://joeyinsync.com/crimson): an international multi-game community that peaked at ~1,400 members, and the staff structure built to outlive its founder. Joey joined as Overseer while it was still Crimson Shield International, then planned and built Crimson Network with its owner, Mikey, and moved into Staff Manager.
- [Site-202 "New World"](https://joeyinsync.com/site202): Joey's own community. A six-day teaser campaign before a single feature shipped, 4,000+ messages on launch day, 100 members in a week, and a founder account compromise the community never felt.

## Writing

Joey is the author of a completed science-fiction novel of approximately 90,000 words and is currently writing his second novel. National-level writing award; Cambridge C2 Grade A (Writing 200/200). He writes every announcement, rule and lore document in his portfolio.
